 Search Netflix vs. Disney+ in South Korea: How Streaming Platforms Are Reshaping the Korean Entertainment Industry
 lewishooper1 9 hours ago 3 min read From blockbuster K-dramas to exclusive original productions, discover how global streaming giants are competing to shape the future of Korean entertainment and take its stories to audiences around the world. Do any of these streaming services stand out above the rest?! 
 Netflix and Disney+ are competing for viewers through Korean original series, exclusive K-dramas, and global entertainment releases. ( Squid Game /Netflix) Korea's entertainment industry has boomed in the past couple of years, and it has been one of the biggest players in global streaming services. 
 With global fan bases becoming addicted to K-dramas and films, production companies are turning their heads towards Asia, in particular Korea, to produce original productions. Big-name international powerhouses such as Netflix and Disney+ continue investing in Korean content; the competition to secure the next global hit is becoming increasingly fierce, and at times too competitive, driving down lower production prices and cast pay-outs. 
 Netflix: Continuing Its Korean Entertainment Takeover 
 Can This Love Be Translated was a big hit in 2026. (Netflix) For a while now, Netflix has been establishing itself in the Korean entertainment industry, and it has relied heavily on investing in its own original productions. 
 Our writer Lewis Hooper has been an extra in some of these productions in the past. Netflix is known for being a major player within the industry, and it's able to turn simple Korean storytelling into a globally recognised entertainment piece. 
 Since Netflix is a global subscription service, it is able to introduce Korean talents and productions into a global marketplace, which once before was not as accessible to international fans. 
 Disney+: Challenging Netflix for the Korean Market 
 The cast of The Remarried Empress at a promotional event in Seoul. (Korea JoongAng Daily) For Netflix to simply take all of the Korean market, it would be unfair and perhaps a little too easy. 
 Disney+ has also been looking to cement its position in the Korean entertainment market, also by producing Korean original dramas as well as opening up franchises and signing partnership deals with big-name K-production companies. 
 For Disney+, their approach, although similar to that of Netflix, has been to build up a portfolio of high-profile productions and dramas, which in turn allows viewers to choose its platform and have the option to binge-watch much-loved classics and new content. 
 Our writer Lewis Hooper has also been an extra in some of the Disney+ productions in Korea and said that the budget and the way that actors are treated on set is very good compared to other production companies. 
 The Battle for Korean Talent and Production Companies 
 With more and more international platforms looking to find their way to the Korean entertainment market, it does open up more and more opportunities for actors, production staff, and also regional services in Korea as well. 
 Since K-dramas have exploded globally and with more and more K-culture fans traveling to Korea, the tourism and entertainment industry can both benefit from each other. 
 This may simply not be possible if foreign big named entertainment companies were not operating in Korea, as their budgets are often larger, and in addition have bigger distribution opportunities and access to audiences that traditional Korean broadcasters may struggle to reach. 
 Fan Opinion: Are Viewers Happy with the Competition? 
 For K-drama fans around the world. having more streaming platforms to choose from is a win-win situation. 
 Bigger production services often mean lower subscription costs, higher-quality productions, and big-name stars. However, some global K-drama fans worry that the once simple storytelling that takes place in a K-drama may get overshadowed and turned into something less authentic. 
 What's Next? The Future of Korean Streaming 
 So what will the future of Korean streaming look like? 
 The Dojeon Media team can definitely see more and more global entertainment companies investing in the Korean entertainment market; the next challenge, however, may be blending more cross-cultural stories together and appealing to both a Korean and international market within the same drama or production. 
 With more high-budget dramas being released within the next few years, this is one step further in maintaining Korea's position in the global entertainment industry. 
 Final thoughts 
 For the Dojeon Media team, although Netflix may have a slight advantage over Disney+ in terms of global reach, it is clear that Disney+ is catching up, since both media platforms have big budgets and original productions being released. 
 It is important that Korean creators and actors, especially use these opportunities to build a name for themselves and create job opportunities domestically.
